nx2e01.title: Born on the cusp: am I both signs?
nx2e01.caption: Born near the line between two signs and never sure which one you are? The Sun is in one sign at your birth minute, and your Moon and rising add the rest. You were never half of anything.

nx2e02.title: Why does the Moon change shape?
nx2e02.caption: Pisces thought a thin Moon meant a sad Moon. Half of it is always lit; we just see it from a new angle each night. A quiet week in love isn't the end of the story either.

nx2e03.title: Why is a half moon called a quarter?
nx2e03.caption: A half-lit Moon is called a quarter because it's a quarter of the way around its orbit. Halfway through anything, a date, a season, a year together, is a lovely time to ask how it's going.

nx2e04.title: Why is the Moon out in the daytime?
nx2e04.caption: Leo wanted the sky to itself, but the Moon is up in daylight on lots of days. If the Moon is feelings, they don't clock out at sunrise. Say the soft thing at noon, not only at 2 AM.

nx2e05.title: Is there a dark side of the Moon?
nx2e05.caption: The far side of the Moon gets just as much sunlight; we simply never see it from here. Everyone you love has a side they haven't shown yet. Let them share it when they're ready.

nx2e06.title: Why does the Moon look huge tonight?
nx2e06.caption: That giant Moon on the horizon is the same size as always; it's a trick of how our brains judge size. Big feelings can do that too. Take a breath and check their real size before you react.

nx2e07.title: Is a blue moon actually blue?
nx2e07.caption: A blue moon is a calendar thing, not a colour, and it only comes around every few years. Kindness shouldn't wait that long. Small sweet things, often, are what people remember.

nx2e08.title: Why isn't there an eclipse every month?
nx2e08.caption: There's a new moon every month but no eclipse, because the Moon's path is tilted and usually slips past. Plot twists are rare. Most of love happens on ordinary days, so make those count.

nx2e09.title: Why does the Moon turn red in an eclipse?
nx2e09.caption: In a lunar eclipse the Moon sits in Earth's shadow, and a little red sunlight still bends in to reach it. Hard weeks can feel like that shadow. Let your people in; some light always finds you.
